public_rationale: CoreWeave reported a quarterly net loss. Nebius reported positive adjusted EBITDA but a net loss from continuing operations. These records show why the definition of profit matters, but they neither prove that every AI-rental provider loses money nor identify a matched, net-profitable counterexample. The unknown accounting basis also prevents a supported or contradicted assessment.
limitations: The search does not establish an exhaustive provider universe.
Company-wide losses can coexist with profitable activities.
The conclusion would be different under a definition that accepts adjusted EBITDA as profit.

public_payload.normalized_proposition: No one appears to profit from renting out AI compute.

statement.excerpt: Despite all of those data centers supposedly being built, nobody appears to be making a profit on renting out AI compute.
statement.document_title: The AI Industry Is Lying To You

from_speaker: nobody appears to be making a profit
our_interpretation: I treat 'appears' as a claim about publicly evidenced profitability, rather than an uncheckable statement of personal belief.

The plain reading is profit attributable to the AI-compute rental activity after relevant costs, including depreciation and financing costs. Positive revenue or adjusted EBITDA alone does not establish this.
Use October–December 2025, the latest completed quarter commonly reportable before the post. Providers with different fiscal calendars are aligned to these dates.
The surrounding post discusses company financial results, but the claim supplies no common accounting convention. Its accounting basis remains unknown.
One verified profitable rental business could defeat the universal statement. Losses at a few providers cannot establish it for everyone.
criteria.support_condition: Comprehensive, comparable public results establish that AI-compute rental providers did not earn positive net profit from that activity during the target quarter.
criteria.contradiction_condition: At least one provider demonstrably earned positive net profit attributable to AI-compute rentals during the target quarter, after relevant costs and without relying on unrelated business or investment gains.

evidence.locator: Use of non-GAAP financial measures, page 4; Q4 Financial Highlights, page 1
evidence.explanation: Nebius reported $15 million of positive group adjusted EBITDA alongside a $249.6 million net loss from continuing operations. The positive adjusted measure is material to an alternative reading of 'profit', but it does not establish net profit from AI rentals.

public_payload.what_would_resolve: Comparable AI-rental accounts for the target quarter, with a stated profit definition and complete cost allocation; one verified net-profitable provider would resolve the universal claim against it.
